summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: California - Penal Code §§ 11164–11174.3 (CANRA – Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act)
California - Welfare & Institutions Code § 300 et seq. (Juvenile dependency proceedings)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 22 - Social Security (DSS Child Welfare Regulations)
Title 11 - Law (DOJ Child Abuse Central Index)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the first clause of Welfare and Institutions Code section 300(b)(1) authorizes dependency jurisdiction on a parent's failure or inability to adequately supervise or protect the child without any separate finding that the parent was neglectful, blameworthy or unfit.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the substantive test a court applies in deciding whether allegations fail and the case must be dismissed.
key_cases.quote: As we explain, this history makes clear that the Legislature did not intend to impose a parental fault requirement in the first clause of section 300(b)(1).

key_cases.case_name: Humphries v. County of Los Angeles
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that California's Child Abuse Central Index listing scheme deprives listed persons of a protected liberty interest under the stigma-plus test without adequate procedural due process, because California provided no meaningful process to challenge or remove a listing.
key_cases.relevance: Bears on what must happen to a registry listing when allegations are not proven or a case is dismissed.
key_cases.quote: The Humphries have asserted the existence of a sufficient liberty interest under the stigma-plus test, of which they may not be deprived without due process of law.

state_agency.name: California Department of Social Services

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
